policy.name: junctionx-2026-context-policy-v2
policy.description: Primitive-level challenge policy; not a certification or a calibrated enterprise risk model.
policy.score_formula: Mean of critical=100, medium=50, resilient=0 over rated, non-offered findings. Unknowns excluded and reported separately.
limitations: A zero score is not evidence of a secure system.
Static calls and declared configuration are not proof of runtime execution.
Unknown primitives, parameters and encrypted handshake fields remain unknown.
The number and duplication of observed primitives affect this heuristic score.
Hash tiers extend the brief with an explicit 128-bit ideal quantum-query target; they are not NIST-assigned risk tiers or practical attack estimates.

evidence.detail: KeyAlgorithm: RSA; explicit key size 2048 bits

caveats: Declared configuration, not proof of runtime use.
findings.explanation: Classical public-key primitive relying on factoring or discrete logarithms; vulnerable to a sufficiently capable quantum computer.
findings.recommendation: Plan a role-appropriate PQC migration. Use a KEM for key establishment and a signature scheme for signatures; do not substitute one for the other.

caveats: Declared configuration, not proof of runtime use.
findings.explanation: Project policy: 256-bit digest assessed using generic quantum collision queries (n/3); generic query exponent 85.3 bits against a 128-bit target. This is a model-based primitive tier, not evidence of a practical break.
findings.recommendation: Check the documented model and usage. Assess signatures, key exchange and secret entropy separately; use a larger digest where the chosen collision-resistance target requires it.

assumptions: Ideal black-box query model; query exponent is not wall-clock attack cost or a NIST security category.

findings.explanation: Project policy: 256-bit digest assessed using generic quantum collision queries (n/3); generic query exponent 85.3 bits against a 128-bit target. This is a model-based primitive tier, not evidence of a practical break.
findings.recommendation: Check the documented model and usage. Assess signatures, key exchange and secret entropy separately; use a larger digest where the chosen collision-resistance target requires it.

assumptions: Ideal black-box query model; query exponent is not wall-clock attack cost or a NIST security category.
Primitive-level 128-bit query target chosen for this project; no protocol or implementation certification.
Conservative collision model for the TLS hash component; HKDF and MAC uses are not independently assessed.

priorities.description: Technical inspection order by primitive and evidence state, not a calibrated enterprise risk ranking. Business impact, asset ownership and confidentiality lifetime are not known.
priorities.ordering: Selected classical public-key mechanisms, configured mechanisms, public-key material/certificate signatures, then static calls; hybrid review, missing information, policy reviews and deployment verification follow. Offered capabilities are inventory-only.

actions.title: Plan public-key migration
actions.reason: A classical public-key mechanism was selected in the captured handshake; complete session security is not established.
actions.next_step: Plan a role-appropriate PQC migration. Use a KEM for key establishment and a signature scheme for signatures; do not substitute one for the other.

actions.title: Review symmetric protection
actions.reason: This primitive is medium under the challenge policy; practical exposure depends on usage and protection lifetime.
actions.next_step: Review confidentiality lifetime and policy; consider AES-256 where appropriate. Separately check modes, nonce handling and key management.

actions.title: Review the project hash model
actions.reason: This tier uses the project's ideal query model and chosen target. It is not a NIST category or evidence of a practical attack.
actions.next_step: Check the documented model and usage. Assess signatures, key exchange and secret entropy separately; use a larger digest where the chosen collision-resistance target requires it.
